The Stained Glass: blocks, ECB, CBC, the confessor

Sealed. The Court's alchemists will cut letters into blocks and push each through a small machine of substitutions and shuffles. When the same block goes in twice, the same block comes out twice, and the picture shows through the glass.
Act II will cover a toy block cipher, ECB mode, CBC bit-flipping and the padding-oracle attack.
Glass shows what's behind it. Remember that.
Sealed. A sigil that stands for a whole letter. Easy to make. Hard to forge. Unless it is small enough to meet its twin.
Act III will cover hash functions, birthday collisions, length extension and HMAC.
A seal proves nothing but that somebody owned wax.
The Court of Primes: numbers that keep secrets
Sealed. Arithmetic on a clock face, and keys that may be shouted from a tower because only a second key can undo them.
Act IV will cover modular arithmetic, RSA and its classic misuses, Diffie-Hellman and discrete logarithms.
Numbers don't lie. The men who pick them do.
Sealed. Men in the middle, clocks that tell tales, a signature that repeats its secret once too often, and a way to prove you know a thing without saying it.
Act V will cover replay and man-in-the-middle attacks, timing side channels, ECDSA nonce reuse and zero-knowledge proofs.
Everything eternal repeats. Even the last trick.
